first_impression.reaction: I went straight to the FAQ and the closing section looking for fees, as I always do. Not much there on money, but the intro didn't oversell. No 'best', no 'dream wedding', and it says the list is unranked and that Smartraveller dates the cyclone seasons. Someone has bothered to cite their sources, so I kept reading.

journey.section: How we chose these Oceania destinations
journey.quote: The list is grouped by region, not by merit, so read it as a map.
journey.reaction: Good. Most of these lists are a 'top 10' that's really a list of who paid. Calling it unranked is honest.

journey.section: How we chose these Oceania destinations
journey.quote: The stations differ in period and in what counts as a rain day: Nadi covers 1961 to 1990, Apia 1971 to 2000 and Hamilton Island 2002 to 2026, so read each figure on its own terms.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of footnote I'd write in a spreadsheet. They're telling me the numbers don't line up perfectly instead of pretending they do. I'll check a couple of the WMO links, but I trust it more already.

journey.quote: The trade-off is water on the ground: flooding is common in downtown Nadi and on the Coral Coast, and it can cut road access to the airport.
journey.reaction: A wedding site telling me the downside of its flagship destination. That's the first thing I'd want to know, and it's sourced to Smartraveller.

journey.quote: Island resorts built around guests who arrive together and stay the week.
journey.reaction: This is the only line in the Fiji section with nothing behind it. It reads like brochure filler next to everything else that's cited.

journey.quote: Can the covered ceremony space and the cyclone postponement terms be written into our contract?
journey.reaction: Useful. These are the questions I'd ask, and they put the risk onto the venue in writing. I'm copying the venue questions into my sheet.

journey.quote: Check with the destination's authorities, or plan a symbolic ceremony.
journey.reaction: I see this line, or something close to it, for Fiji, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Tonga. Honest that there's no official page, fine, but after the third time it feels like the part where I'd need a planner is exactly the part that's left blank.

journey.quote: Exercise a high degree of caution in New Caledonia due to the risk of civil disorder and violence.
journey.reaction: They quoted the government advice directly instead of softening it. Respect for that. Most sites would have left it out to protect a listing.

journey.quote: The Registrar of Marriages issues the licence three days after notice, unless a waiver is granted, and it expires after three months.
journey.reaction: Concrete steps, timings and the ministry linked. This is what I'd want for every country.

journey.quote: For November 2025 only, Earth Sciences New Zealand's summary of that month records a nationwide 15.9°C, a new November record and 2.2°C warmer than the 1991 to 2020 normal.
journey.reaction: Every other entry gives me a long-run average. New Zealand gets one record-breaking month. At least they say 'November 2025 only', but it doesn't help me pick a month. Feels like they didn't have the data.

journey.section: Oceania wedding destinations at a glance
journey.quote: | Fiji | Melanesia | Cyclone season November to April (Smartraveller); January to March wettest at Nadi (WMO) | Check with the destination's authorities | [Fiji guide](/destinations/oceania/fiji) |
journey.reaction: The table is the most useful thing on the page. Source named in each cell. I'd screenshot this.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is the one big promise on the page and there's nothing behind it. And 'payments' is where my alarm goes off. If they handle the payments, do they take a cut from the venue? The page doesn't say.

journey.section: Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Advisor quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Better than nothing. Written fee up front is a good sign. But I still don't know whether it's a flat fee, a percentage, or whether suppliers pay them commission. That's the question I'd ask on the first call, and I'd rather read the answer here.

unanswered_questions: How is the planner fee calculated: flat, percentage of budget, or something else?
Do you take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers, and is it disclosed to me?
When the Advisor 'handles payments', whose account does the money go through?
What exactly does the fee include, and what counts as extra?
For Fiji, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Tonga, will you actually work out the legal steps for us, or is that on us?
Is there a real Pacific wedding with its actual budget I can look at?
What does New Zealand look like as a long-run average by month, not one record month?
If a cyclone postpones the wedding, what is your own cancellation or rebooking policy, separate from the venue's?

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported sweeping claim ('anywhere in the world') on a page that is otherwise careful, and it mentions payments without saying anything about commissions.

turn_offs_found.quote: Island resorts built around guests who arrive together and stay the week.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild brochure language with no source, in a section where everything else is cited.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the at-a-glance table and the venue questions
A mate planning a Pacific wedding who asked about cyclone season

cta_reaction.quote: Tell [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=oceania-wedding-destinations&utm_content=closing) which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling.
cta_reaction.why: The CTAs come after the evidence, not before, which I appreciate. The page earned some trust. But my main question, what the fee buys and whether you take a cut from suppliers, isn't answered here, so I'd probably check reviews and a fee page first before handing over my details.
